notes: Primary contact: Maya R. (Dir of CX Automation) - pragmatic, cares about reliability over feature novelty.
Pain: agents spend 40-60% of time on non-value work (ticket triage + drafting replies across languages). Need agent-assist templates + fast, accurate translation.
POC scope: automated ticket summary + suggested replies, auto-ticket tagging, one-click tool-calls (create incident, escalate), and locale-aware reply tone models.
Performance targets discussed: mean reply-gen latency <= 650ms for agent-assist UI, 99th pct tail <= 1.2s; sustained throughput target 200 rps in peak region, burst up to 800 rps during campaigns.

Cost: cost-sensitivity moderate; willing to pay for Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable latency but need clear cost-per-conversation math. Asking for Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.

Model preferences: open to community models if quantized and latency-friendly; want fallback path to smaller low-cost model for non-critical summarization. Interested in model pinning per locale (EU customers -> EU residency models).

Routing: locale-based routing required (detect language + route to EU-hosted Dedicated or private nodes). Also need tone profiles by locale (formal vs conversational) and ability to override per account.

Tooling: must integrate with Zendesk (primary), ServiceNow (escalations), Slack notifications, and internal case-mgmt via REST 'create_ticket' tool-call. Need reliable tool-call retries and idempotency guarantees.

Security: mandatory SSO/SAML, audit logging of model outputs, customer-managed KMS for key material, retention rules per region, and option for private control plane or on-prem for regulated EU customers.
Quotes from stakeholder: 'We need replies that sound native — not just literal translations.' — Maya R.
Technical concerns from infra: KV cache warmup during spikes; want automatic warm cache warming and pre-warming policy for holiday campaigns.
Open risk: escalation path for hallucinated tool-calls; they demand explicit human-confirm flows for ticket creation above certain confidence thresholds.
Support artifacts: shared Drive PoC deck, security FAQ. Fireflies meeting notes capture tone examples (links above).
Next POC ask: run 48h resilience test on a Dedicated pool with EU private nodes and demonstrate end-to-end ticket creation with retries under simulated downstream failures.
CSM note: if POC shows SLA + security alignment, likely to go to procurement Q2 2026 (forecast 2026-05).
